design.text: Randomized, multi-center, double-masked, active comparator (aflibercept)-controlled, 2-year studies; patients randomized 1:1 to aflibercept 2 mg Q8W after three initial monthly doses or VABYSMO 6 mg every 4 weeks for the first 4 doses followed by dosing up to every 16 weeks (Q16W).

citations.quote: The safety and efficacy of VABYSMO were assessed in two randomized, multi-center, double-masked, active comparator-controlled, 2-year studies (TENAYA – NCT03823287 and LUCERNE – NCT03823300) in patients with nAMD.

Patients were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to one of two treatment arms: 1) aflibercept 2 mg administered fixed every 8 weeks (Q8W) after three initial monthly doses; and VABYSMO 6 mg (0.05 mL of 120 mg/mL solution) administered by intravitreal injection every 4 weeks (approximately every 28 ± 7 days, monthly) for the first 4 doses, followed by optical coherence tomography and visual acuity evaluations 8 and 12 weeks later to determine whether to give a 6 mg (0.05 mL of 120 mg/mL solution) dose via intravitreal injection on one of the following three regimens: 1) Weeks 28 and 44; (also referred to as Q16W dosing); 2) Weeks 24, 36 and 48 (also referred to as Q12W dosing); or 3) Weeks 20, 28, 36 and 44 (also referred to as Q8W dosing).

population.text: Newly diagnosed, treatment-naive patients with neovascular (wet) AMD; ages 50 to 99, mean 75.9 years.

citations.quote: A total of 1,329 newly diagnosed, treatment-naive patients were enrolled in these studies, and 664 patients received at least one dose of VABYSMO. Patient ages ranged from 50 to 99 with a mean of 75.9 years.

endpoint.text: Mean change from baseline in BCVA (ETDRS letter score) averaged over the week 40, 44, and 48 visits; non-inferiority margin of −4 letters.

citations.quote: Both studies demonstrated non-inferiority to the comparator control (aflibercept) at the primary endpoint, defined as the mean change from baseline in Best Corrected Visual Acuity (BCVA) when averaged over the week 40, 44, and 48 visits and measured by the Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) letter chart.
The lower bound of the 95% confidence interval for the mean change in BCVA could not be lower than minus 4 letters to declare non-inferiority.

target_moa.text: Humanized bispecific antibody that inhibits two pathways by binding VEGF-A and Ang-2; VEGF-A inhibition suppresses endothelial cell proliferation, neovascularization and vascular permeability, while Ang-2 inhibition is thought to promote vascular stability.

citations.quote: Faricimab is a humanized bispecific antibody that acts through inhibition of two pathways by binding to VEGF-A and Ang-2. By inhibiting VEGF-A, faricimab suppresses endothelial cell proliferation, neovascularization and vascular permeability. By inhibiting Ang-2, faricimab is thought to promote vascular stability and desensitize blood vessels to the effects of VEGF-A.

modality.text: Bispecific (humanized bispecific IgG1 antibody, CrossMAb format)

citations.quote: Faricimab-svoa is a humanized bispecific IgG1 antibody that binds vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A) with one arm and angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2) with the other arm.
Faricimab is a humanized antibody of the CrossMAb format that binds vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF) and angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reaction (≥5%) was conjunctival hemorrhage (7%). Other common reactions (≥1%) included vitreous floaters (3%), retinal pigment epithelial tear (3% AMD), intraocular pressure increased (3%), eye pain (3%), and intraocular inflammation (2%). Potentially serious risks include endophthalmitis and retinal detachments, increase in intraocular pressure, and thromboembolic events.
